items.title: Test flake with broken pipe while unpacking from `ecosystem-test-caches`
items.reason: Open canonical match: a registry source distribution fails during streamed extraction with the same archive, member-specific unpack, and response-body errors. Its broken pipe is the same class of interrupted stream as astral-sh/uv#21641's connection reset.

items.title: Retrying in case of a broken pipe
items.reason: Historical user-facing match involving large PySpark source distributions and the same streamed member-unpack failure. It was closed after the reporter reduced its CI frequency, not because sdist resumption was implemented.

items.title: Retry streaming downloads on broken pipe errors
items.reason: This retry fix was prompted by astral-sh/uv#12359. The new log shows that retrying occurs and exhausts its budget, so the fix is relevant history but does not resolve repeated interruptions.

items.title: Python installation fails during streamed unpack with connection reset error
items.reason: It has an almost identical extraction and connection-reset chain, but concerns `uv python install`; its fixes are scoped to managed Python and binary downloads, not registry package sdists.

items.title: Support resumable downloads
items.reason: It describes uv restarting interrupted downloads while pip can resume, matching the robustness gap here. It is broader than streamed sdist extraction and was closed by a wheel-focused implementation.

items.title: Retry failed partial downloads with HTTP Range header when supported
items.reason: This fix resumes interrupted wheel downloads with HTTP range requests. Repository code places it in `download_wheel_response`, while registry sdists still stream directly into the extractor, so it does not cover this path.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using `wxpython`, `Invalid tar file`, `failed to unpack`, `error decoding response body`, `error reading a body from connection`, `connection reset`, and `broken pipe`. Conceptual and fix-oriented searches covered registry sdists, streamed archive extraction, retry exhaustion, interrupted downloads, resumption, and HTTP range requests. astral-sh/uv#14171 was ruled out as the canonical tracker because it is Python-download-specific; astral-sh/uv#21570 is wheel-only. astral-sh/uv#15896 concerns Artifactory TLS/server behavior, while astral-sh/uv#2138 concerns Azure Artifacts index behavior.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#13717 is open and tracks the same underlying failure: a transport error interrupts a registry sdist while uv streams it into the tar extractor, producing a member-specific unpack error. Broken pipe versus connection reset is only a low-level transport variant. This is not a regression of astral-sh/uv#13281 because the new log shows three retry delays and four fresh requests, nor of the Python-specific fixes for astral-sh/uv#14171.
summary: astral-sh/uv#13717 is the closest open match. astral-sh/uv#12359 and astral-sh/uv#13281 document the same sdist stream failure and retry handling; astral-sh/uv#14171 is a Python-download analogue, while astral-sh/uv#16934 and astral-sh/uv#21570 concern resumable downloads but currently implement recovery only for wheels.
draft_response:
This is the same streamed source-distribution download failure tracked in astral-sh/uv#13717. The final causes show that the PyPI response is interrupted by a connection reset while uv is unpacking it; the changing member path and successful local-tarball install indicate that the tar file itself is not the problem.

Your verbose log also shows that uv retries the complete download three times before failing. astral-sh/uv#21570 added partial-download resumption for wheels, but source distributions are still unpacked as they stream, so that change does not cover this path. We'll keep the source-distribution case centralized in astral-sh/uv#13717; your wxPython reproduction provides another user-facing example.
